board:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original art-direction board for Thousand Unit Skirmish, a medieval frontier RTS.
Create one beautiful cohesive landscape-format environment kit illustration on warm ivory paper, with a large assembled orthographic terrain vignette across the upper half and six well-spaced isolated modular asset studies below. Painterly art direction, sculpted broad shapes, deliberate visible brushwork, legible chunky silhouettes at distant strategy-game zoom. Grounded old frontier, inviting mossy sage and olive greens, warm ochre earth, slate gray stone with warm lit edges. Slightly storybook but mature and restrained. No photorealistic noise, no pixel art, no cartoon outlines.
Upper scene: a winding worn dirt track through quiet grassy meadow, passing an organically connected curved rock escarpment with varied heights, capped ends and a grassy top. One mature broad oak and two sparse tapered pine trees frame open space suitable for armies. Give cliff faces broad interlocking fractured stone masses; a little moss in seams. No buildings or soldiers. No floating island or thick square tile bases. The scene is a painted preview of potential assets, not a screenshot.
Below: six isolated individual studies, arranged clearly in two rows of three, labeled in small understated dark typography exactly: "CLIFF STRAIGHT", "CLIFF CORNER", "CLIFF END", "LOW OUTCROP", "OAK", "PINE". Same material family throughout. Three cliff modules should look like pieces of one kit with comparable height and continuous top edge, corner turns 90 degrees, end tapers down. Each object shown fully with margin, no overlaps between studies. Three-quarter orthographic view about 46 degrees above ground, soft upper-left light, minimal contact shadows. Emphasize authored shape and quiet ground over tiny texture detail. Top title exactly "FRONTIER / ENVIRONMENT STUDY". This is a review board; no invented UI, no watermarks.
cliff: Create a standalone Meshy image-to-3D source illustration based on the CLIFF STRAIGHT study in the previous environment board. Exactly one modular straight rock cliff segment, all visible, centered with generous margins on a pure plain white background. No other objects, text, labels, border, paper texture, landscape or scenery. Preserve the board's slate gray fractured stone, warm ochre highlights, restrained mossy olive grassy cap and mature painterly treatment. Broad sculpted interlocking rock masses and clear readable silhouette, not photoreal noise. Segment proportions about 4 units long, 1.5 units deep, 2 units tall; level top with thin grassy cover. Full volume with visible top, front and right end in three-quarter orthographic view from about 46 degrees elevation. Ends approximately vertical and compatible with another segment of equal height; no tapered ends, ground slab, floating island, large grass skirt, trees or bushes. Small integral basal stones only. Diffuse neutral studio illumination, minimal shadow, no directional cast shadow outside object. Designed as a 3D reconstruction reference for rendering eight consistent views, not as a tile texture.
